meta.title: Where the turns went
meta.description: Corrected forensics on the A1/A2 baseline after the overnight gold migration

props.title: Where the turns went
props.subtitle: The missing gold is fixed. The honest pass rate is 76.5 percent, and it went down because the truth got counted.

props.content: An earlier version of this page reported 420 turns with no readback gold and a 90 percent pass rate. Both numbers were captured 21 minutes before the gold migration landed and are withdrawn. This revision measures the current corpus.

props.title: Measured 00:04, now withdrawn
props.content: A1 scored 67 of 765 rows at 14.9 percent. A2 scored 23 and passed none. 420 turns carried no readback gold. Headline 90.0 percent over 1102 scored turns.

props.title: Measured 08:50, current
props.content: A1 scores 413 rows at 36.8 percent. A2 scores 93 at 29.0 percent. 3 turns carry no readback gold. Headline 76.5 percent over 1518 scored turns.

props.label: Verdict
props.title: One problem solved, two still standing
Missing gold is essentially closed
props.content: Two waves landed overnight. The first copied 862 spoken-form readbacks verbatim from expected_readback into expected_radio_speech_text across 46 files, so the projector reads the field authors were actually writing. The second added 203 workflow-authored readbacks. Missing gold went from 420 turns to 3.

props.title: The callsign substitution got worse
props.content: 21 of 91 comparable A2 rows now run under a callsign that disagrees with their own gold: the scenario declares N31862, the runtime speaks N17XX. It was 11 rows before the waves. A1 remains clean at 0 of 340.

props.title: BATC is still excluded by name
props.content: batc_operator_practice_v1 sits in the corpus directory with 17 turns and 25 fixtures in the ledger, removed by a hardcoded frozenset before corpus routing. No skip message, no entry in skipped_corpora, no comment giving a reason. Unaffected by the gold waves.

props.label: Mechanism
props.title: The acceptance filter has exactly three exits
props.subtitle: A turn is scored only if none of these fire

props.content:
The first two exits are settled policy. Pilot own-emissions never enter the voice module, and ambient party-line traffic is not addressed to us.

The third exit was the whole problem. It does not describe the turn — it describes a hole in our own data, and a turn landing there stopped counting while still failing. That is what produced the fake 90 percent.

It is now nearly empty. Three turns remain in A1 and none in A2. The exit should stay in place as a tripwire, but it no longer distorts the score.

props.label: Arithmetic
props.title: Current denominators, by reason
props.subtitle: Counts from the run's own rows

props.content:
The headline fell from 90.0 to 76.5 percent, and that is the migration working. The scored denominator grew by 416 turns; only about 169 of them pass. The old rate was high because it was computed over the turns that happened to have gold.

Excluded-and-failing turns dropped from 519 to 105, and every one of the 105 is now a pilot own-emission or ambient row — categories where a fail verdict carries no meaning. The invisible-failure problem largely dissolved with the gold fix rather than needing its own remedy.

props.label: Missing corpus
props.title: BATC is two things, and neither is in the baseline
props.subtitle: One by design, one by a hardcoded frozenset

props.content:
The parameterized set is a deliberate holdout, run by its own recipe against a different scenarios directory and excluded from the headline on purpose. That one is correct.

The operator-practice scenario is the open question. It has audio, transcripts, and 17 authored turns, and it is removed by name with no diagnostic. Whatever the original reason, silent name-based removal is the same absence-without-explanation pattern the projector work just eliminated.

props.label: Dominant failure
props.title: Readback text is now the biggest bucket
props.subtitle: 138 failures across A1 and A2, and most are real

props.content:
This corrects an earlier claim on this page. Before the gold waves the readback failures looked dominated by spelling and callsign artifacts. Against the full 138-row set they are not: convention accounts for 22 percent, and 77 percent are real differences in what the readback says.

Thirteen rows fail on punctuation and casing alone, which is worth a separate look at comparison strictness before anyone touches gold.

The five-versus-fife class is not a units question. The units workstream carries a JP-confirmed ruling from today that bare canonical magnitude is the stored form for slots with the unit implied by the typed domain, and its boundary note explicitly exempts stored eval gold, which stays hand-authored spoken text under gold independence. Spoken text has two independent producers by design, and nothing currently forces them to agree.

props.label: Open defect
props.title: A callsign the harness supplies over the one the scenario declares
N31862 against N17XX
props.claim: PlaneEnglish scenarios are scored against readbacks spoken by the wrong aircraft.
props.evidence: 21 of 91 comparable A2 rows carry gold ending Warrior Three One Eight Six Two while the runtime speaks November One Seven X-ray X-ray. The scenario files declare callsign N31862. A1 shows 0 mismatches across 340 comparable rows because its scenarios are authored around N17XX, so the disagreement never surfaces there.
props.source: baseline-now.json, per-row callsign tail comparison; modules/config/schema.py:784 declares callsign default N17XX
props.limitation: The default value is confirmed present. The path by which it wins over Scenario.callsign has not been traced end to end, so the fix location is a hypothesis.

props.title: Fix the A2 callsign
props.content: Trace why Scenario.callsign loses to the config default. It is the largest single mechanical cause left in A2 and it grew, not shrank, through the gold waves.

props.title: Look at the 13 punctuation-only failures
props.content: Rows that differ only in commas and casing should not be failing a text gate. Check comparison strictness before proposing any gold change.

props.title: Attack the 107 content differences
props.content: This is the real work and it is now the biggest bucket in both corpora. Dropped segments and collapsed clearances, not spelling.

props.title: Unmask or delete the BATC scenario
props.content: Give the deny-list entry a documented reason and a visible skip message, or let the scenario rejoin A1.
